notes: Equivalent correct approach with good doc updates; tests are broad (latency, status_text, dynamic name), but the status_codes and escaped-literal request-only cases would also pass on the old code, and the latency test depends on timing.

A clean AST walk with a dynamic flag, matching the reference semantics; tests cover request-only variants, status text, direct `ph()` calls, dynamic names and a latency-based retry, though the `status_codes` request-only case is a weak check because the placeholder is never set.

Closest to the reference, reusing isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall and isCELStringLiteral with a clean isResponsePlaceholder helper; it returns the internal slice uncopied (documented), and the predicate table, including mixed matcher sets, plus the integration tests are thorough.

Reuses the existing `isCELCaddyPlaceholderCall` and `isCELStringLiteral` helpers to collect placeholder names and the dynamic flag, closely mirroring the reference; tests include a table-driven unit test of the matcher-set classifier (including mixed sets) plus end-to-end POST and direct `ph()` tests.

Correct AST-based detection exposed through a predicate API; the extra value-type MatchExpression case and the 'rp.' prefix fallback are speculative and never reached, while the tests are carefully built to fail on the old behavior (e.g. setting the status_codes placeholder value).

Correctly records placeholder names at provision time from the AST, treats non-literal names as dynamic, and only evaluates response-referencing expressions; it also adds an unneeded `rp.` prefix match and a value-type MatchExpression case, but its tests are thorough (it sets the lookalike `status_codes` value so a wrong evaluation would match).

Records the placeholder names from the checked CEL AST, flags non-literal names as dynamic and filters on the exact response placeholders plus the header prefix; the tests cover every case the maintainers listed, though the doc edit drops the {rp.is_transport_error} mention.

Correct and well documented, but it silently skips (rather than marking dynamic) `ph` calls with an unexpected arg count, which is unreachable in practice; it also reorders struct fields needlessly, and its GET/POST test writes `gotBody` from the handler goroutine without synchronization.

Works for the main zip and squashfs cases, but zip skips the extra suffix for a symlink whose name already ends in .rclonelink, so such a link gets the wrong name; the sync-based escape test is weak and may be order-dependent, and the squashfs tests depend on mksquashfs being installed.

The main flow works and List and NewObject agree. However, the zip path skips the .rclonelink suffix for any symlink whose own name already ends in .rclonelink, so it is exposed under the wrong name; in squashfs, NewObject prefers the trimmed symlink over a same-named regular file.

Fixes both zip and squashfs correctly, matches the reference semantics, adds the suffix even to symlinks whose names already end in .rclonelink, and tests listing, NewObject, range/seek, roots and a hostile-archive copy; the squashfs root-resolution code is a bit convoluted, it also accepts unsuffixed root names, and its squashfs tests skip when mksquashfs is missing.

A clean fix close to the reference for both zip and squashfs, which also correctly handles symlinks whose names already end in the suffix and roots with or without the suffix; the regular-file/symlink name collision is left unresolved, as in the reference.

Correct and thorough, including resolving collisions between a symlink and a regular member of the translated name, with strong tests and a committed squashfs fixture; however it decompresses every zip symlink target at mount time, which is costly on remote storage, and it adds shared helpers in archiver.go plus doc changes beyond what was needed.

The most thorough fix: regular members win name collisions consistently in List and NewObject, links are found only under their suffixed name, and the tests are strong. Its main drawbacks are eagerly reading every zip link target at mount time (costly on remote backends) and adding shared helper surface.

Squashfs reads --links from each call's context instead of capturing it at New (consistent with the failing hidden test), drops empty-target symlinks, rewrites unrelated existing log messages, and adds a new internal package plus zip hiding of members under symlinks even without --links, all beyond the spec.

Defensively drops members inside symlinks and resolves name collisions, but it fails a hidden test and squashfs reads --links from the per-call ctx instead of New's. It also drops empty-target symlinks and rewrites existing, unrelated log messages.
